document.title: Start Here — Health in Timor-Leste
document.caveat: Describes published policy, which can differ substantially from practice. Check locally.

sections.title: Rezumu Ezekutivu (Tetun - tradusaun makina / machine translation)
National guidelines, policies and key documents

contestedFigures.status: CONTESTED - sources move in opposite directions. Do not quote a single figure.

contestedFigures.indicator: Current health expenditure as % of GDP
contestedFigures.status: CONTESTED, and the indicator itself is misleading for Timor-Leste.

values.source: WHO country profile / SEARO SDG profile
values.figures: 11.4% (2021) - not reproducible from primitives; implies a non-oil GDP denominator

contestedFigures.guidance: Use US$ per capita (144.21 in 2023) and health as a share of government expenditure (9.16% in 2023). The GDP ratio moved because petroleum GDP fell 43%, not because spending changed.

keyFacts.note: 13 municipalities plus RAEOA. Atauro separated from Dili on 1 January 2022. Documents saying 12 or 13 predate that.

keyFacts.fact: Out-of-pocket share of current health expenditure
keyFacts.note: Among the lowest in the world. No social health insurance; public care free at point of use.

keyFacts.value: US$138.3 million, 6.04% of the state budget

keyFacts.note: 14% of the health budget, spent treating Timorese patients abroad.

keyFacts.value: 6 hospitals, about 71 community health centres, 344 health posts

keyFacts.note: Among the highest in the world.

keyFacts.value: South-East Asia Region (SEARO), NOT Western Pacific

keyFacts.note: WHO's own planning database still lists the superseded 2011-2030 plan.
What WHO and others call the "integrated health services programme".
Formerly SAMES. Documents saying SAMES are out of date.
ms.gov.tl returns 502; moh.gov.tl dead since 2020. The live channel is Facebook (139,000 followers) and a document portal at apps.ms.gov.tl.

keyFacts.value: INSP-TL approval required for all clinical research and any training longer than 3 days

knownGaps: No 3W (who does what where) dataset and no health-cluster partner list for Timor-Leste.
No current national HRH plan (2020-2024 expired, no successor published).
National clinical guidelines largely date from 2004-2010.
Whether the December 2023 national TB prevalence survey results were published is unverified.
